captions.headline: We built this because businesses deserve real hiring systems.

And yet most of those hires still happen through email threads, WhatsApp groups, shared Google Sheets, and LinkedIn DMs that never get a proper follow-up.

We have seen this firsthand. A founder posts a role, gets 60 applications in three days, loses track of who said what in which email chain, and eventually makes a hire based on whoever happened to stay in touch at the right moment. That is the problem RisePoint Careers was built to solve.

Not for enterprise. Not for HR departments with dedicated recruiters and procurement budgets. For the founder who is managing client work and operations and hiring between meetings. For the practice manager at a 12-person clinic trying to fill a front-desk role without dropping the rest of the job. For the agency owner hiring their third account manager while simultaneously billing their biggest client.

Q3 hiring season is here. If you are a small business planning to add headcount between now and September, the pipeline starts today. Not with a better job posting. With a system that lets you run a fair, organized process without adding hours to your week.

That is what we built. And that is why we built it.

captions.headline: Build your talent pool now, before the pressure makes you settle.
captions.subline: The SMB hiring mistake that costs the most.
captions.caption_linkedin:
Many small businesses enter Q3 in reactive hiring mode. A key person leaves, a contract expands, or growth arrives faster than expected, and suddenly you are scrambling to fill a role while still running the business.

That is when most SMB hires go wrong.

Right now, most small businesses are in what analysts describe as a low-hire, low-fire holding pattern. They are not expanding headcount aggressively, but they are also not cutting. The businesses that move fastest when Q3 volume picks up are the ones who are not starting from zero when a seat opens.

Trade Secret No. 27: build a light talent pool before you have an opening.

Here is what that looks like in practice. When you meet someone strong at a networking event, or review an application that is solid but poorly timed, log them. A name, a role type, a brief note on why they stood out, and a rough date when you might be ready to talk. That is it. No complex system required.

When a seat opens and you are under pressure, you will have three people to call instead of thirty applications to sort. That difference can mean weeks off your time-to-hire.

Spark Careers Enterprise makes this automatic. Every candidate you engage with stays organized and searchable, even the ones you are not ready for yet. Your pipeline is there when you need it, without the spreadsheet archaeology.

Q3 hiring season runs April through September. You are in it now.

captions.headline: Your resume is being scored before a human reads the first word.
captions.subline: Format. Keywords. Structure. Three things that decide your score.
captions.caption_facebook:
Trade Secret No. 27: AI screening tools reject approximately 75 percent of resumes within seconds of submission. Most of the time, the issue is not your qualifications. It is formatting, keyword alignment, or column structure.

By mid-2026, an estimated 83 percent of employers use filters specifically designed to flag resumes that appear AI-generated or fail to match the job description closely enough.

Three things to check before you apply. One: is your resume a single column? Two-column layouts regularly break when parsed by ATS software. Two: does your resume include keywords from the actual job posting, not just general industry terms? Three: did you tailor the content to this specific role, or is it the same document you sent everywhere?

Spark Careers walks you through all three. Take the free scan and see where your resume stands.

https://spark.risepointcareers.com/?utm_source=social&utm_medium=post&utm_campaign=w27-tue-b2c
captions.caption_instagram:
AI tools reject about 75 percent of resumes in seconds. Here is what they flag, and how to get through.

Most rejections are not about your qualifications. They are about formatting, keyword gaps, or a two-column layout that the ATS cannot parse.

Before your next application, check three things. First: is your resume single-column? Two-column designs regularly fail ATS parsing. Second: does your resume mirror the language in the job posting? Not stuffed with keywords, just aligned to how the employer describes the role. Third: is the document tailored to this specific job, or is it a general template?

By mid-2026, most employers use filters that flag both poor formatting and generic content. Personalization and structure matter more now than they did a year ago.

Spark Careers walks you through all of it for free.

captions.headline: Hiring through email and DMs is not a system. It is a liability.
captions.subline: Built for founders who are doing the hiring themselves.
captions.caption_linkedin:
There is a particular kind of hiring that happens at small businesses. It goes something like this.

You post a role. Applications come in. You read some of them when you have a moment, which is rare. A few candidates email to follow up and you mean to reply but forget. Someone reaches out on LinkedIn and you save their profile to look at later. Two weeks go by and you realize you have 47 applications, three conversations going in three different places, and no clear picture of where any of them stand.

Then you make a hire based on who was easiest to get in front of you at the right moment. And six months later, you are not sure it was the right call.

This is not a failure of judgment. It is a failure of tooling.

Enterprise ATS platforms were not built for this problem. They were built for HR departments running coordinated hiring across dozens of open roles with dedicated recruiters and structured workflows. BambooHR, Workable, Greenhouse: all excellent for what they were designed for. None of them were designed for the founder who is their own recruiter.

Spark Careers Enterprise was. It keeps all your candidates in one place, lets you move them through a simple pipeline, and sends updates automatically so no one falls through the cracks. You can run a fair, organized process in the time it used to take you to find that one email.

If your current hiring system is your inbox, this was built for you.
